Most learners review new words on the same day they meet them, then wonder why the words vanish by Friday. Studies of memory keep pointing the same way: recall that happens after a night of sleep, when the trace has partly faded, leaves a far stronger mark than recall that happens while the page is still open.

Why does spaced review beat same-day review?
choices: Because the memory trace has partly faded, so recall has to work harder
Because words studied at night are easier to read the next day
Because sleep makes the material feel more familiar on the page
Because reviewing later takes less time than reviewing immediately
items.a: Because the memory trace has partly faded, so recall has to work harder

items.q:
Psychologist Robert Bjork argues that some obstacles during practice are 'desirable difficulties': they slow down visible progress while quietly strengthening what stays in memory. A practice session that feels smooth can therefore be producing less learning than a session that feels like a struggle.

What does the phrase 'desirable difficulties' suggest?
choices: Teachers should remove obstacles so practice feels smooth
Difficult materials are always more effective than easy ones
Struggle during practice can strengthen long-term retention
Progress that feels slow is a sign of poor practice methods
items.a: Struggle during practice can strengthen long-term retention

items.q:
Readers often mistake the ease of rereading a chapter for evidence that they know it. The pages feel familiar, the argument arrives without effort, and a test the next morning reveals how little survived. Familiarity, researchers warn, is a poor proxy for knowledge.

The passage implies that learners who feel fluent while rereading ___.
choices: have stored the chapter durably in long-term memory
often mistake familiarity for genuine knowledge
should switch to harder chapters immediately after
benefit most from reviewing the same chapter again
items.a: often mistake familiarity for genuine knowledge

items.q:
A study team compared three revision schedules across a term. Learners who reviewed a topic the day it was taught rated their confidence highest, yet scored lowest on the delayed final. The group whose reviews began only when material started to slip performed best, despite reporting the most effort during practice.

Which sentence best captures the study's conclusion?
choices: Review works best while the material still feels fresh
Confidence during revision predicts final performance
Effortful practice is a symptom of a poor study schedule
Review pays off most when it starts at the edge of forgetting
items.a: Review pays off most when it starts at the edge of forgetting
